facts: On September 30, the coach said Ronaldo, 41, would not start. Jorge Jesus: "No player will ever make a decision for me."

UEFA rules made someone wear No. 7. Each team lists 23 players, numbered 1 to 23, so every number is used. It is not a permanent change.
caption:

Very simply put: the coach benched Ronaldo. The rulebook moved his shirt.

facts: Players challenged 10,557 calls in the robot's first season. The robot overturned 5,686 of them: 54% (AP, October 2).
Catchers win 59% of their challenges. Pitchers win only 40%. Batters win 49% (AP).
On September 30, a challenge ended a playoff game. A first. Phillies at Braves, 10th inning: a called ball became strike three. The Braves still won the series.
12 Hawk-Eye cameras track every pitch. Sony owns Hawk-Eye. The data runs on a private 5G network. Margin of error: about one-sixth of an inch.
Only the batter, pitcher or catcher can challenge, by tapping their cap. Not the manager. Each team gets 2 a game and keeps any it wins.
Human umpires still call every pitch. The robot only answers challenges, in about 15 seconds (MLB).
The zone runs from 27% to 53.5% of the batter's height. 17 inches wide, at the middle of the plate. A pitch is a strike if any part of the ball touches it.
MLB measured players before noon, because people shrink during the day. No shoes, no hats, heels together, back against the wall (MLB.com, AP).
caption:
"robot" — 500+ searches today. Baseball's robot umpires finished their first season, and the numbers are in.

Why: In MLB's first season of ball-strike challenges, players challenged 10,557 calls. The robot flipped 5,686 of them, 54%. On September 30, a challenge ended a playoff game for the first time: a called ball became strike three for the Phillies in Atlanta.

What most people don't know: there is no single strike zone. Each hitter's zone is set by his own height, measured without shoes, from 27% to 53.5% of it. MLB measured players before noon, because people shrink during the day.

Very simply put: in baseball, your height is now part of the rulebook.

facts: About 1 in 8 US women will get breast cancer. About 1 in 43 will die of it (American Cancer Society).
In 2026, the US expects 321,910 new invasive cases in women. And 42,140 deaths. Plus 60,730 early, non-invasive cases (DCIS).
Men get it too: about 2,670 US cases a year. About 530 deaths in 2026. A man's lifetime risk is about 1 in 755.
Caught before it spreads, 5‑year survival is over 99%. 92% overall, 32% once it has spread far (women diagnosed 2015 to 2021, ACS).
The death rate is down 44% since 1989. About 546,000 deaths avoided through 2023 (American Cancer Society).
More than 85% of women diagnosed have no family history. American Cancer Society, October 1, 2026. No family history does not mean no risk.
New cases are rising fastest in women under 50. 1.4% a year from 2013 to 2022, against 0.7% for women 50 and older (ACS).
Its maker refused to share the peach ribbon. So they chose pink. Charlotte Haley, 1991. Self magazine's lawyers said a new colour needed no permission. Pink launched in October 1992.
caption:

Why: The American Cancer Society expects 321,910 new invasive breast cancers in US women in 2026, and 42,140 deaths. About 1 in 8 US women will get it. Caught before it spreads, 5-year survival is over 99%. The death rate is down 44% since 1989.

Very simply put: the pink ribbon started as a workaround.

Very simply put: those blurry words you typed helped digitize books.

angle: On October 1, 2026 Greg Lui (Yiu Kong Lui), 38, CEO of Earthmade Computer in California, was arrested on a 3-count indictment returned September 29 in the Central District of California (case 2:26-cr-00618): conspiracy to violate the Export Control Reform Act, outbound smuggling, and money-laundering conspiracy; DOJ says more than $300 million of export-controlled servers (Nvidia A100, H100, RTX 4090 and 5090) were sent to China after he allegedly told US server makers the end users were in Malaysia and Singapore; more than $176 million came from two Malaysian firms in 2024, one a lumber and plywood company per the indictment; one January 2024 shipment of 27 H100 servers was worth about $7.6 million; maximum 20 years each for conspiracy and laundering, 10 for smuggling; not convicted; earlier cases: about $510 million (Supermicro co-founder, March 2026), $160 million (December 2025); export controls since October 2022; hidden fact: in fiscal 2025, 18% of Nvidia's revenue was billed to Singapore but under 2% shipped there; Nvidia says customers centralize invoicing there and over 99% of controlled data-center revenue billed there was for US-based customers (Nvidia 10-K, TechCrunch).
facts: On October 1, Greg Lui, CEO of Earthmade Computer, was arrested. Indicted September 29 in Los Angeles federal court on 3 counts. He has not been convicted.
Prosecutors say he claimed the buyers were in Malaysia and Singapore. Then the servers allegedly went on to China, with false export papers.
The servers held Nvidia H100 and A100 chips, controlled since 2022. Plus RTX 4090 and 5090 graphics cards, prosecutors say.
One shipment alone: 27 H100 servers worth about $7.6 million. Los Angeles to Kuala Lumpur, January 2024, according to the indictment.
Two Malaysian firms paid his company more than $176 million. January to October 2024. One was a lumber and plywood company founded in 1999 (indictment).
He faces up to 20 years on each of two counts. Conspiracy and money laundering. Smuggling carries up to 10 (Department of Justice).
Not the first case: one server scheme topped $510 million. A Supermicro co-founder was charged in March 2026. Another network: $160 million, December 2025 (DOJ).
Singapore was 18% of Nvidia's revenue on paper. Under 2% shipped there. Fiscal 2025, by billing location. Nvidia says customers invoice through Singapore and the products ship elsewhere.
caption:
"greg lui doj charges" — 50,000+ searches this week. A California seller is accused of sending $300 million of Nvidia servers to China.

Why: On October 1, Greg Lui, CEO of Earthmade Computer, was arrested in Los Angeles on 3 counts. Prosecutors say he told US server makers the buyers were in Malaysia and Singapore, then shipped the servers on to China. He has not been convicted.

What most people don't know: in fiscal 2025, 18% of Nvidia's revenue was billed to Singapore, its No. 2 market on paper. Less than 2% shipped there. Nvidia says over 99% of its controlled data-center sales billed there were for US-based customers.

Very simply put: where chips are billed isn't where they go.

caption:

Very simply put: AI writes code. It can't wire a data center.

facts: Verity opened at No. 1 with about $32.6 million. US and Canada, October 2 to 4 estimates. $62.5 million worldwide (The Numbers, Box Office Mojo).
Dakota Johnson plays a writer hired to finish Verity's books. Anne Hathaway is Verity Crawford, an author badly hurt in a car crash. Josh Hartnett plays her husband.
It beat Tom Cruise's Digger, which opened with $8 million. Cruise's worst opening since Lions for Lambs in 2007 (TheWrap).
It's Anne Hathaway's third No. 1 movie of 2026. After The Devil Wears Prada 2 and The Odyssey (Variety).
It cost $40 million, the most of any Colleen Hoover film. It made that back 1.5 times over worldwide in its first 3 days.
Only about 1 in 3 critics liked it. Audiences gave it 70%. Rotten Tomatoes. Opening-night audiences gave it a C+ CinemaScore.
The ending was chosen after test screenings. The filmmakers tried several endings and dropped a darker one. Hoover: "Those screenings really helped" (Variety).

caption:
"verity movie" — 500,000+ searches this week. The Colleen Hoover thriller is America's No. 1 movie.

Why: Verity, with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson, opened with an estimated $32.6 million in the US and Canada and $62.5 million worldwide. It cost $40 million. Only about 1 in 3 critics liked it. Tom Cruise's Digger opened with $8 million.

facts: The Treasury started mailing $500 checks on September 30. The White House announced the "Working Families Obamacare Refunds" on September 10.
More than 950,000 people in 30 states get one. About 139,000 in Texas and 127,900 in Florida, the only state counts released (Newsweek).
Each check comes with a letter from Trump. "That money belongs to hard-working Americans, not the Government," it says (CBS News).
It's $500 per person. Nobody has to apply. Payment is automatic, so one household can get several checks.
Only people who paid full price qualify. No tax credits. Most earn over 400% of the poverty line: $62,600 alone, $128,600 for a family of 4.
20 states and DC get nothing. They run their own exchanges, so the federal government never collected the fee there, an official told ABC News.
The money comes from a fee built into premiums. HealthCare.gov charges insurers a user fee: 1.5% of premiums in 2025, 2.5% in 2026, 1.9% in 2027 (CMS).
Only about 1 in 20 marketplace buyers qualify. 950,000 out of 19.2 million people paying for plans in February 2026 (ABC News, KFF).
caption:
"trump aca refund checks" — 500,000+ searches this week. More than 950,000 Americans are getting $500 each.

Why: On September 30, the Treasury began mailing $500 checks to people with HealthCare.gov plans in 30 states. The White House calls them refunds of excess HealthCare.gov fees. They are automatic and paid per person, so one family can get several.

What most people don't know: only about 1 in 20 marketplace enrollees qualify. You must have paid full price, with no tax credits, in a state that uses HealthCare.gov. The other 20 states and DC run their own exchanges, so people there get nothing.

Very simply put: most people searching for this check won't get one.

facts: Italy's president made the first Italian state visit to Monaco. Sergio Mattarella, October 2 and 3. "It is indeed the first time," said Prince Albert II.
At the state dinner: Elie Saab silk and Graff diamonds. A one-shoulder beaded gown, with diamond hoop-and-fringe earrings from Graff's Gypsy collection.
She was born in Zimbabwe, then called Rhodesia, in 1978. Charlene Wittstock, born in Bulawayo on January 25. Her family moved to South Africa when she was 11.
She swam for South Africa at the 2000 Olympics. Sydney. Her 4x100 m medley relay team finished 5th in an African record time (Olympedia).
She met Prince Albert in 2000, at a swim meet in Monaco. They married in 2011 in the palace Throne Room, where Italy's state dinner was held.
Nearly 1 in 5 Monaco residents is Italian. 7,559 of 38,857 at the end of 2025. Yet no Italian president had made a state visit before.
Her engagement ring is by Repossi, a jeweler founded in Turin. She wore it to greet Italy's president. The couple first appeared in public at the 2006 Turin Olympics.
Gabriella was born 2 minutes before Jacques. He is the heir. December 10, 2014. Monaco's constitution gives "priority" to males among siblings (Article 10).
caption:
"charlene princess of monaco" — 500+ searches today. Italy's president just made the first state visit to Monaco.

Why: On October 2 and 3, Sergio Mattarella became the first Italian president to make a state visit to Monaco. Prince Albert II and Princess Charlene hosted him with their 11-year-old twins. At the state dinner she wore a one-shoulder Elie Saab gown and Graff diamond earrings.

What most people don't know: her daughter, Princess Gabriella, was born 2 minutes before her twin brother, Jacques. But Jacques is the heir. Monaco's constitution gives males priority among siblings.

Very simply put: in Monaco, being born first isn't enough.

facts: Novig's ad with Sydney Sweeney launched September 9. "Just Sports." She says "sports" 16 times and never names one (Daily Bruin).
She's not just the star. She's an equity partner. And creative director: she oversaw the music, camera angles and script (Fortune). Her stake isn't public.
Olympic swimmer Ariarne Titmus called it "an absolute joke." British runner Amy Hunt: "it's 2026. Stop sexualizing women in sport."
After the ad, Novig's trading volume rose nearly 94%. 20 days after launch vs 20 days before, the company told CNBC. First-time depositors: up 218%.
"Ultimately, I think we have nothing to apologize for," says its CEO. Jacob Fortinsky, to CNBC on October 3. He founded Novig in 2021, in his senior year at Harvard.
Novig is reportedly raising money at a $2 billion value. The Wall Street Journal, September 30. In February it was valued at $500 million (Front Office Sports).
It's an exchange: you trade against other users, not a bookie. The CFTC approved it as a federal contract market in June 2026. Users must be 21 (Covers).
It works in California and Texas, where sports betting is illegal. It says state betting laws don't apply to a federal exchange. Ohio, Missouri and Connecticut told it to stop.
caption:
"novig commercial" — 10,000+ searches this week. Sydney Sweeney's ad for a sports prediction app keeps getting louder.

Why: Novig's "Just Sports" ad, starring Sydney Sweeney, launched September 9. On October 3, the company told CNBC its trading volume rose nearly 94% in the 20 days after launch. Its CEO said: "Ultimately, I think we have nothing to apologize for."

facts: Harry Kane won his 125th England cap on October 6. England 3-0 Czech Republic at Wembley. He scored twice and forced an own goal (Sky Sports).

facts: On October 6, ASOS users got a push alert: "ASOS HACKED." "Dear Asos DPO and IT, we have fully compromised the Snowflake instance. Engage with us, or we will leak it."
ASOS: names and contact details may have been accessed. Through third-party platforms it uses to message customers. It does not believe cards or passwords were hit.
ASOS shares closed down 10.6% that day. At 449p. In April 2021 they peaked at 5,772p (Yahoo Finance, City AM).
ASOS has 16.4 million active customers. At the end of its 2026 financial year. It started in London in 2000 as "AsSeenOnScreen."
The hackers call themselves Xuanye. They're brand new. Their Telegram channel was created that day. Sophos found no earlier mention on hacker forums (The Next Web).
Snowflake: "no compromise" of its platform. "We have found no compromise of the Snowflake platform," it said. ASOS hasn't confirmed the hackers' claim.
The 2024 Snowflake breaches hit about 165 organizations. At AT&T, call and text records of nearly all cell customers were stolen. Ticketmaster was hit too.
They never broke into Snowflake. They used stolen passwords. Mandiant: at least 79.7% leaked through infostealer malware, some from 2020, on accounts without two-factor login.
caption:
"asos hacked" — 20,000+ searches this week. ASOS app users got a push alert from hackers.

Why: On October 6, ASOS app users received a notification titled "ASOS HACKED," claiming the hackers had "fully compromised the Snowflake instance." ASOS says names and contact details may have been accessed, but it does not believe cards or passwords were. Its shares closed down 10.6%.

What most people don't know: the big 2024 "Snowflake hack" never broke into Snowflake. Mandiant traced it to stolen passwords, at least 79.7% leaked through infostealer malware, on accounts without two-factor login. Snowflake says it has found no compromise of its platform this time either.

Very simply put: in 2024, the hackers didn't break in. They logged in.

facts: The new term opened with a climate case. Suncor v. Boulder, argued October 5. A decision is expected by the end of June 2027 (ABC News).
Boulder sued Suncor and ExxonMobil in April 2018. Boulder County and the City of Boulder, Colorado. They want the companies to pay part of local climate costs.
Colorado's top court let the case go ahead, 5‑2. May 12, 2025. Federal law doesn't block Boulder's claims, it ruled.
The companies call it an "unprecedented effort". "...to use state law to regulate global conduct," said their lawyer, Kannon Shanmugam. The Trump administration backs them.
Roberts: a win could bring lawsuits in "every single state." "If you prevail, the next day, a municipality in every single state will file a lawsuit," he told Boulder's lawyer.
The companies say nearly 60 governments have filed similar suits. From their brief. In January 2025 the Court declined to stop Honolulu's suit.
Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside. No reason given. AP reports he holds ConocoPhillips and Phillips 66 stock, but not Suncor or Exxon.
With 8 justices, a 4‑4 tie lets Boulder's case go ahead. The Colorado ruling would stand. Boulder needs 4 votes; the oil companies need 5 (SCOTUSblog, ABC News).
caption:
"supreme court" — 2,000+ searches today. The new term opened with a fight over who pays for climate change.

Why: On October 5, the Supreme Court heard Suncor v. Boulder. Boulder, Colorado, sued Suncor and ExxonMobil in 2018 to make them pay part of its local climate-change costs. The companies, backed by the Trump administration, say state law can't be used to regulate global emissions. The justices sounded divided.

What most people don't know: only 8 justices will decide, because Justice Samuel Alito stepped aside. A 4-4 tie would leave Colorado's ruling in place, and Boulder's case would go ahead.

Very simply put: Boulder needs 4 votes. The oil companies need 5.

facts: The UN made October 4 to 10 World Space Week in 1999. UN General Assembly resolution 54/68, adopted December 6, 1999.
October 4, 1957: Sputnik 1, the first satellite, reached orbit. A metal ball about 58 cm wide with 4 antennas. Pictured: a full‑size model.
Sputnik beeped for only about 3 weeks. Then its batteries died. It kept circling Earth silently until it fell back on January 4, 1958.
October 10, 1967: the Outer Space Treaty took effect. Not the day it was signed. It opened for signature on January 27, 1967.
This year's theme: "Rocket Revolution." Organizers point to "increased space access and falling launch prices."
In 2025, Falcon 9 flew 165 times: about half of all launches. One booster has now flown 37 times. Pictured: 2 Falcon Heavy boosters landing, 2018.
Getting to orbit got about 20 times cheaper per kilogram. Space Shuttle: about $54,500 a kg. Falcon 9: about $2,720 (NASA analysis, 2018).
No country can own the Moon. A 1967 treaty says so. Article II: it "is not subject to national appropriation by claim of sovereignty." 118 countries are parties.

What most people don't know: no country can own the Moon. Under the 1967 treaty, the Moon "is not subject to national appropriation by claim of sovereignty." 118 countries are parties, including the US, China and Russia.

Very simply put: countries can visit the Moon. None can own it.

angle: Margaret Hamilton, who led the MIT team that wrote the on-board flight software for Apollo's command and lunar modules, died Sept 30, 2026, at 90 (MIT announced Oct 7; daughter Lauren confirmed to AP Oct 8; NASA's Jared Isaacman tribute). Apollo 11: 1202/1201 program alarms minutes before touchdown on July 20, 1969; the priority-driven software restarted, dropped low-priority jobs and kept the landing going. Hidden fact: her young daughter crashed MIT's command-module simulator by selecting P01 mid-flight; Hamilton wanted a safeguard and was told 'Astronauts are trained never to make a mistake'; Jim Lovell did the same on Apollo 8 (Christmas Day 1968: 'It was my goof'); her fix was adopted. facts: Margaret Hamilton died on September 30, at 90. MIT announced it on October 7. Her daughter Lauren confirmed it.
She led the team that wrote Apollo's on‑board flight software. For the command and lunar modules, at MIT. She joined MIT's Apollo work in 1965.
In her famous photo, the stack of paper is code. Printed listings of her team's Apollo software, 1969. It stood head‑high. She was 5 foot 4.
Minutes before the Moon landing, the computer flashed 1202. July 20, 1969: the computer was overloaded. Her team's software restarted, dropped low‑priority jobs and kept the landing going.
She helped make the term "software engineering" popular. "When I first started using this phrase, it was considered to be quite amusing," she said.
The program was woven by hand, mostly by women. Core rope memory, made at Raytheon near Boston: a wire through a core was a 1, around it a 0. She was the "rope mother."
Apollo's computer had 72 kilobytes of fixed memory. Plus 4 kilobytes of working memory, says the National Air and Space Museum.
Her daughter crashed the simulator. Then astronaut Jim Lovell did it. She was told "Astronauts are trained never to make a mistake." Lovell did it on Apollo 8, Christmas Day 1968. Her fix went in.
caption:
"margaret hamilton" — 20,000+ searches this week.

Why: Margaret Hamilton, who led the MIT team that wrote the on-board flight software for NASA's Apollo missions, died on September 30, at 90. MIT announced it on October 7. In 1969, minutes before the first Moon landing, the overloaded computer flashed alarms. Her team's software kept the landing going.

facts: Even the Post Office calls it "non‑widely observed". It became a federal holiday in 1971, so post offices close. But many businesses stay open and keep mailing, its 2026 memo says.

Columbus landed on October 12, 1492. Nobody knows exactly where. He named the island San Salvador. Its people called it Guanahani. It is in the Bahamas, but which island is still argued.
He never reached the US mainland. His 4 voyages reached the Caribbean and Central and South America. In 1493, his crew landed on St. Croix and Puerto Rico, now US territory.

The first national Columbus Day was not on October 12. President Benjamin Harrison set it for Friday, October 21, 1892, the 400th anniversary. His order: "Let the national flag float over every schoolhouse in the country."
The Pledge of Allegiance was written for that celebration. Francis Bellamy wrote it for the 1892 school program. Children across the country first said it at Columbus Day ceremonies that October.
The first state to make it a holiday dropped it in 2020. Colorado made Columbus Day a state holiday in the early 1900s. In 2020, it swapped it for Cabrini Day, the first Monday in October.

17 states and DC also honor Native Americans that day. South Dakota went first, in 1990. Berkeley was the first city, in 1992. Indigenous Peoples' Day is not a federal holiday. Count: Pew Research, 2025.

facts: Two quakes hit the ridge on October 13, 6 hours apart. First M6.7, then M6.8, says the USGS. It first posted the second one as 6.9, the number in many headlines.

No tsunami warning. NOAA said there was no danger. Its words: "There is no tsunami danger for the U.S. east coast, the Gulf of America states, or the eastern coast of Canada."
The seafloor slid sideways. That rarely makes a tsunami. Fault data shows both quakes moved sideways. The USGS says sideways slip barely lifts the seafloor, so the tsunami risk is small.
The ridge is about 16,000 km long, mostly underwater. It runs from Iceland to near Antarctica. It is part of a 65,000 km ridge system, the longest mountain range on Earth, NOAA says.
The Atlantic grows about 2.5 cm a year. Roughly as fast as your fingernails grow, the USGS says. The plates on each side of the ridge drift apart a little every year.
M6‑plus quakes hit the ridge about 2 times a year. 56 since 2000 in the USGS catalog (our count). On October 13, 1925, an M7.1 hit the northern part of the same ridge.
Marie Tharp found its rift in 1952. He called it "girl talk." Her colleague Bruce Heezen dismissed her idea at first, in her own words. Then earthquake locations lined up inside her valley.

facts: Nobody was hurt. The whale swam away. It happened off Moriches Inlet, near Fire Island, on October 9 or 10 (reports differ). The 34‑foot boat was still seaworthy, ABC7 reported.
The crew had already cut the engine. They saw the whale feeding on bunker fish about 300 yards away. An expert said shutting down was the right move.
A local group has logged 500 humpbacks around New York. Gotham Whale, since its catalog began in 2012. It now records 80 to 100 a year, up from 10 to 30 a year before 2018.
They come for one fish: bunker. Also called Atlantic menhaden. Catch limits have been in place since 2013, and a 2025 check found it is not overfished.
Most humpbacks near New York are young. Often less than 5 years old, a Rutgers study found. On October 7, two young humpbacks got stuck on Fire Island sandbars. Both swam free.
93% of humpbacks hit by boats here were juveniles. A 2021 Stony Brook study of the waters off New York. Young whales feed close to shore, where boats are busiest.
270 humpbacks have died on the Atlantic coast since 2016. NOAA calls it an Unusual Mortality Event. 50 of them were in New York. About 45% of the 129 examined showed a boat strike or entanglement.
Off New York, the 100‑yard distance is advice, not law. For humpbacks it is law only in Hawaii and Alaska. New York's advice: put the engine in neutral when whales come close.

facts: Falcon 9 lifted off at 6:33 a.m. on October 13. From Cape Canaveral, Florida, carrying NASA's CRS‑35 cargo mission to the space station. The booster flew back and landed next to the pad.
The rocket was in sunlight. The ground was still dark. The sun lit up its exhaust high above. That glowing shape is the "jellyfish," NASA's Kennedy Space Center says.
In thin air, the exhaust spreads wide. High up, the plume grows far wider than the rocket itself. That wide glow is the bell of the jellyfish.
It only happens near sunrise or sunset. In full dark, the plume isn't lit up. In daylight, it doesn't stand out. Pre‑dawn and after‑dusk launches make it often.
People saw it as far north as Virginia. Photos came from Florida, Georgia, the Carolinas and Virginia. The rocket flew northeast, up the coast, to match the space station's orbit.
It looked like it was falling. It wasn't. The rocket follows the curve of the Earth on its way to space, NASA explains. From the ground, that bend looks like a drop.
Dragon carried over 6,300 pounds to the space station. Including the last 2 of 8 new roll‑out solar arrays. It docked on October 15 and stays until mid‑November.
In 1977, a rocket "jellyfish" was reported as a UFO. The Soviet news agency TASS described a glowing "jellyfish" over the city of Petrozavodsk. It was a launch from a secret Soviet rocket base.

facts: Milwaukee swept the champion Dodgers 4 games to 0. The Dodgers won the 2024 and 2025 World Series. Game 4 ended 6‑4 at Dodger Stadium on October 15.
A year earlier, the Dodgers swept them. In the 2025 NLCS, Milwaukee scored 4 runs in 4 games. No MLB team had ever swept back the team that swept it.
They trailed in every game and still swept. No team had done that in a best‑of‑seven series. In Game 4 they came back from 4‑0 down.
They won 103 games, the most in baseball. A franchise record, for manager Pat Murphy, 67. He was the National League Manager of the Year in 2024 and 2025.
Their payroll ranks 19th. The Dodgers' ranks 2nd. MLB.com calls Milwaukee baseball's smallest media market.
In 1982 they led the World Series 3 games to 2. Then they lost Games 6 and 7 in St. Louis, 13‑1 and 6‑3. It was called the "Suds Series": two beer cities.
In 1998 they moved to the National League. The first team in the modern era to switch leagues. This is their first National League pennant.
Their blue and gold came from Seattle. The Seattle Pilots were sold out of bankruptcy a week before Opening Day 1970. No time for new uniforms, so Milwaukee wore theirs.
caption:
"world series" — 2,000,000+ searches this week.

Why: On October 15, the Milwaukee Brewers finished a 4-0 sweep of the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers and won their first National League pennant. They host Game 1 of the World Series on October 23, against Cleveland or Tampa Bay. The Brewers have never won a World Series.

What most people don't know: the Brewers' blue and gold are a hand-me-down. The team was bought out of bankruptcy as the Seattle Pilots a week before Opening Day 1970. There was no time for new uniforms, so Milwaukee started out in Pilots uniforms.

Very simply put: swept last year. Swept back this year.

caption:
"street fighter movie" — 500,000+ searches this week.

Why: "Street Fighter," the new live-action movie from Legendary and Capcom, opened at No. 1 in North America this weekend with $31 million, and $51.1 million worldwide (studio estimates, October 18). Critics gave it 42% on Rotten Tomatoes. Audiences gave it 79%.

What most people don't know: the first Street Fighter arcade game, in 1987, came in a deluxe version with no attack buttons. You punched two big rubber pads, and the harder you hit, the harder your fighter hit. Players hurt their hands, and the six-button version took over.

Very simply put: players punched the machine. Now critics punch back.

The 2017 wait was 5 to 6 weeks. This one is about 100 days.

Very simply put: same sentence. Longer wait.

caption:
"the legend of zelda" — 20,000+ searches this week.

Why: Nintendo's remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time comes out on November 5, only on Nintendo Switch 2. This week Nintendo posted a new overview trailer, and the first hands-on previews went live. For the first time, Link can jump with a button, and you can hum his ocarina songs into the console's microphone.

What most people don't know: the game's lock-on sword fighting was sparked by a ninja show. On a hot summer day, the developers ducked into a playhouse at Toei Kyoto Studio Park to cool off, and watched ninjas attack a samurai one at a time. "If we hadn't gone, we wouldn't have hit on the system," designer Yoshiaki Koizumi said.

Very simply put: the highest-rated game ever, thanks to a hot day.

facts: Trump: New Mexico should rename itself "New America." On Truth Social, October 19: "New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America. We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America!"
It's at least the third time he has raised it. A map with "Mexico" crossed out on September 6. Then, in a video on October 3: "Hello, New America, formerly known as New Mexico."
A president can't rename a state. New Mexico's constitution, Article I: "The name of this state is New Mexico." A change needs a majority of each house of the legislature, then the voters.
The governor: the name "isn't up for debate." Michelle Lujan Grisham, September 6. The state's Republican nominee for governor said: "New Mexico does not need a new name."
It became the 47th state on January 6, 1912. After nearly 62 years as a territory, longer than any other in the lower 48. Its capital, Santa Fe, dates to 1610: the oldest state capital.
Its license plates have said "USA" since 1969. Added so people in other states would know where it is. New Mexico Magazine has printed readers' mix‑up stories since 1970.

In 1906, Congress passed a law making it part of "Arizona." One state named Arizona, with Santa Fe as its capital. New Mexico voted yes. Arizona voted no. Congress had also floated "Lincoln" and "Montezuma."
The name "Nuevo México" is older than the country of Mexico. Spanish explorers were using it by 1581. Mexico took its name at independence in 1821, 240 years later.
caption:
"new mexico" — 2,000+ searches today.

Why: On October 19, President Trump posted on Truth Social that "New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America." It was at least the third time he has raised it. A president can't rename a state: New Mexico's name is written in its constitution, and changing it takes the state legislature and then the state's voters.

What most people don't know: the name is older than the country of Mexico. Spanish explorers were calling the region "Nuevo México" by 1581. Mexico took its name when it won independence in 1821, 240 years later.

Very simply put: New Mexico had the name 240 years before Mexico.

Very simply put: judge a recall by its class, not its pounds.

The US tried year‑round daylight time in 1974. Nixon signed it in December 1973. Approval fell from 79% to 42% over dark winter mornings, and standard time came back that October.

Its first big champion was Chris Martin's ancestor. William Willett, a British builder and the Coldplay singer's great‑great‑grandfather, pushed it from 1907. He died in 1915, a year before Britain adopted it.

Very simply put: a movie villain who began as a movie actor.

Vivek Ramaswamy, 41, Republican. Amy Acton, 60, Democrat. Ramaswamy founded the drug company Roivant Sciences and ran for president in 2024. Acton, a physician, was Ohio's health director from 2019 to 2020.
Fox News poll: Acton 50%, Ramaswamy 48%. Within the margin. 1,592 likely voters, October 15 to 19, margin of error 2 points. Marist had Acton up 50% to 43%. ActiVote had Ramaswamy up 51% to 49%.
Two forecasters now rate it Lean Democratic. Sabato's Crystal Ball on October 22, the Cook Political Report on October 23. Ohio last elected a Democratic governor in 2006.

Pro‑Ramaswamy ads outspend pro‑Acton ads more than 2 to 1. AdImpact, early October. Acton raised more from donors in July, August and September. Ramaswamy has put in over $36 million of his own money, as loans.
There is no debate. Acton said no. Ramaswamy, September 2: "I challenge Amy Acton to join me on the debate stage." Acton, October 20: she will "not normalize my opponent's behavior."

Either way, a first: the first woman, or first Indian American, elected. Acton would be Ohio's first woman elected governor; Ramaswamy, its first of Indian descent. Nancy Hollister served 11 days in 1998 and 1999 but was never elected.
Neither candidate has ever held elected office. Not a city council seat, not a state seat, not Congress, NPR and AP report.

"vivek ramaswamy" — 1,000,000+ searches this week. The 9th biggest search in the US.

Why: Ohio picks a new governor on November 3. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, 41, faces Democrat Amy Acton, 60, for the seat Mike DeWine must leave because of term limits. Most October polls show Acton ahead, a few show Ramaswamy ahead, and two forecasters moved the race to Lean Democratic this week. No debate is scheduled.

What most people don't know: neither candidate has ever held elected office. And either way it's a first: the first woman, or the first person of Indian descent, elected governor of Ohio.

Very simply put: their first elected job would be the top one.
